messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: Request for output of command line parameters, and problems with c*.st* files
parts:
(1) We don't do this but you have a point. It should be easy to save this info somewhere. I'll take a look and perhaps we can get it in the forthcoming 2.2 update. The full "scenario" parameters are saved in the irace.Rdat file (this is the real log file), but they are not saved as a command-line, so you don't know what changed from the default. Note that you can also use --debug-level >= 1, it will print all scenario parameters (again, not the command-line, so you have a point).

(2) Is the location where "c1-13.stdout" is written an NFS (network-shared) partition? If so, there may be some delay. It may be worth it to write the file to a local-drive /tmp directory, then move it to the shared drive, save in a log somewhere the location of the file in /tmp so that if it crashes you can check that the file was really in /tmp and it was really not empty. If it is network delay issue, you may need to add "sleep 1" or a while loop checking for the file (the template for target-runner inst/templates/target-runner.tmpl contains an example of this commented out)

Is there anyway to check that your program didn't crash and it actually finished successfully? Perhaps make it print "OK" to stderr just before exit, save the output of all runs and see if when it fails, there is a corresponding OK. Also, as the user-guide says:

12.3 My program works perfectly on its own, but not when running
under irace. Is irace broken?
Every time this was reported, it was a difficult-to-reproduce bug in the program, not in irace.
We recommend that in targetRunner, you use valgrind to run your program. That is, if your
program is called like:
$EXE ${FIXED_PARAMS} -i $INSTANCE ${CONFIG_PARAMS} \
1> ${STDOUT} 2> ${STDERR}
then replace that line with:
valgrind --error-exitcode=1 $EXE ${FIXED_PARAMS} \
-i $INSTANCE ${CONFIG_PARAMS} 1> ${STDOUT} 2> ${STDERR}
If there are bugs in your program, they will appear in $STDERR, thus do not delete those files.

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] Re: Request for output of command line parameters, and problems with c*.st* files
parts:
On 07/03/17 01:37, M. Wagner wrote:
> (1) It would be awesome if this makes it into irace 2.2 :) I have not touched
> irace.Rdat and (without looking into it now), I am just not sure everything
> will be fine in this file because multiple instances of irace run in the same
> directory. Maybe everything is fine with multiple parallel runs, though.

Not really, they will get overwritten. Irace is designed to separate the setup
and the execution directories, so that you can use the same setup files and
execute multiple runs of irace in parallel (and each run itself parallelized).
This will prevent the output files from being overwritten. See how
bin/parallel-irace does it. You can also tell irace to use a different
location/file (--log-file).

The log file is extremely useful, it contains every configuration sampled,
every experiment made, recovery data, version info, seeds used, etc.
Programmatically parsing the output of irace is not really advisable. We are
happy to improve this if you have some specific suggestions, but using the log
file is much more convenient.

Cheers,

Manuel.

On 11/03/17 03:50, M. Wagner wrote:
> FYI: irace waited itself to death and nothing happend for days. Apparently
> there is a bigger problem here. Alright, I will check the valgrind approach next.

If the file is never non-zero and the sleep is within a loop, then as far as
irace can tell, your program is still running and perhaps doing something useful.

We have not implemented any timeout in irace. I'd like to offer this option,
but I haven't found a portable way to do this with R and users can always use
some OS-specific command, such as 'timeout' in Linux. I'm open to suggestions
on how to do the same in R...

> Fun stats: only 16 of 72 irace runs (3 days each maximum, on 32 cores) were
> successful due to my Heisenbug :(

irace tends to be really good at finding hard-to-replicate bugs in target
algorithms :)

Cheers,

Manuel.

>> Fun stats: only 16 of 72 irace runs (3 days each maximum, on 32 cores) were
>> successful due to my Heisenbug :(
>
> irace tends to be really good at finding hard-to-replicate bugs in target

Btw, if you don't care about the bugs, or you believe that they do not affect
the results of the algorithm and they are simply are hard-drive/memory issue
and you are in a hurry, you could try the option --target-runner-retries to
just tell irace to retry a few times before giving up. Within your
target-runner, just check whether the output is complete, if not, just "exit
1", irace will notice that target-runner failed and re-try.

Cheers,

Manuel.
